model_annotation: The line plot compares the performance of five methods—FT, IKE, MEMIT, ROME, and an unlabeled black line—across three discrete evaluation points labeled “-1”, “-2”, and “-3” on the x-axis, which likely represent increasing difficulty, iteration steps, or dataset splits. The y-axis, unlabeled but scaled from approximately 0.4 to 1.0, appears to represent a normalized metric such as accuracy or success rate. ROME (green line with square markers) shows the strongest upward trend, starting near 0.5 at “-1” and rising to nearly 1.0 at “-3”. MEMIT (purple line with diamond markers) also increases steadily from ~0.5 to ~0.85. The black line (no label, circular markers) rises modestly from ~0.4 to ~0.6. FT (blue line with downward-triangle markers) and IKE (red line with upward-triangle markers) show similar moderate growth, starting near 0.45 and ending around 0.7–0.75. All lines are connected with solid lines and show consistent positive trends, with ROME clearly outperforming the others across all points.
